title: The Dodecanese and Chios: island Greek of the south-east
lead: Ask an old Kalymnian if they are leaving before Easter and you may hear **«'εφ φεύγω μπρι τηλ λαμπρή»**: 'I'm not leaving before Easter'. Every consonant bends towards the next one, final **-ν** survives, and **π** before **ρ** turns into **μπ**. The Dodecanese lie far from Athens and close to Asia Minor, and for centuries they were a no man's land between Byzantium and the Arabs, then the possession of the Knights of St John, the Ottomans and Italy. They joined Greece only in 1948. Their speech is a close relative of Cypriot, and it changes from island to island and sometimes from village to village.
facts: Rhodes, Kastellorizo, Karpathos, Kasos, Chalki, Tilos, Nisyros, Symi, Kalymnos, Astypalaia, Kos, Leros; Patmos is closer to Cretan.

Trudgill: **south-eastern** (Rhodes, Karpathos, Kos, Kasos, Kastellorizo, Leros, with Cyprus) and **eastern** (Symi, Tilos, Nisyros, Kalymnos, Astypalaia, with Ikaria, Chios and the nearby Asia Minor coast).
Rhodian poems from the 14th and 15th centuries, such as Emmanuel Georgillas's «Θανατικόν της Ρόδου», on the plague of 1498.
1947–48, after Italian rule (1912–1943) and a brief German and British occupation.
Receding under Standard Greek and emigration; still strong among older speakers and in remote villages such as Olympos on Karpathos.

timeline.text: Arab fleets raid the Aegean. The historian Robert Browning notes that the Dodecanese were long 'a kind of neutral ground between Byzantium and the Arabs', and that their main dialect features were probably fixed then.
The **Knights of St John** rule Rhodes and Kos. The medieval town of Rhodes is theirs; Greek remains the language of the islanders, and Rhodian poets write in their own dialect.
Ottoman rule, with wide local self-government in many islands. Sponge-diving and shipping (Kalymnos, Symi, Kastellorizo) take islanders across the Mediterranean.
Italy takes the islands in the Italo-Turkish war. In the 1930s it imposes Italian in schools and public life. Italian loans and many Italian-built buildings remain.
Union with Greece. Schooling, radio and later television bring Standard Greek to every island, and the dialects begin to retreat.
Mass emigration. So many people from Kastellorizo moved to Perth and Sydney that far more people of Kastellorizian descent now live in Australia than on the island.

Standard
rows: **ρθ, ργ, βγ** harden to **ρτ, ρκ, βκ**
κκ, ππ, ττ pronounced [kx, pf, tθ]
[tʃ] for κ before ε, ι (some places)
[j] after a consonant becomes [s, ʃ] or [ʒ]

sections.after: Put the features together and you get the Kalymnian sentence from the introduction: **δεν** loses its δ ('εν), its final ν assimilates to φ ('εφ φεύγω), **πριν** becomes **μπρι**, and **την** assimilates to λ (τηλ λαμπρή).

Dodecanese
Standard
rows: Augment kept even unstressed, often as **η-**

sections.after: All four features are shared with Cypriot, and the **-ουσι(ν)** endings go back to the Koine (λύουσι). The **η-** augment is a medieval innovation, found also in Crete and the Cyclades.

sections.text: Chios, Ikaria and the Asia Minor coast opposite them (Smyrna, Çeşme, Ayvalık before 1922) belong with Symi, Kalymnos and Astypalaia in Trudgill's **eastern** group: they share the southern vowel system and many south-eastern traits, but not every Cypriot one. The Greek of the Asia Minor coast moved to Greece with the refugees of 1922–23 and mixed into the new urban speech of Athens, Piraeus and Thessaloniki, while Chios kept its own village varieties. Chiot is famous for its distinctive local vocabulary and for the medieval mastic villages, but it has been studied far less than Cypriot or Cretan, and modern descriptions are few.

notes: **Rhodes**: the largest island, with clear differences between the town and the villages of the south.

**Karpathos**: the north, above all **Όλυμπος**, is one of the most conservative places in the Greek world, with women's traditional dress still worn daily and improvised **μαντινάδες** sung to lyra and lute.
**Kalymnos**: strong assimilation across word boundaries, as in the introduction.
**Symi**: a careful study by Zachariou-Mamalinga (1994) shows how quickly the dialect gave way to Standard Greek after union in 1948.
**Patmos**: closer to Cretan than to its neighbours.

culture.text: Kalymnos was the capital of Mediterranean sponge-diving, and its divers carried Kalymnian speech to Tarpon Springs in Florida, where a Greek community still lives from sponges. On Karpathos, improvised rhyming couplets, **μαντινάδες**, are sung at every feast, much as in Crete. Rhodes and Kos keep the Italian period in their architecture and in a layer of Italian words.
